statusDetail: Coverage-complete report-only audit of six representative paths. Not covered: authenticated account/history and actual third-party merchant checkout, because credentials and purchases were out of scope.

paths.description: Homepage and initial closure notice; global navigation, preferences, security, performance, accessibility, and no-JS behavior.
Representative listing archetype for browsing shops, categories, filters, card grids, and responsive layout.
Representative merchant detail and primary outbound shopping journey, also used for repeated-scroll memory testing.
Representative editorial/notice page for the announced service closure and readable long-form content.
Synthetic nonexistent route to exercise HTTP/navigation failure recovery.
Authentication entry redirect to d Account, inspected for permission timing and modern-auth signals; no credentials submitted.

findings.summary: The site remains light when the user requests a dark color scheme.
findings.evidence: The preferences screenshot is pixel-identical in appearance to the default light capture, and the CSS probe found no prefers-color-scheme rule.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven light/dark surface, text, border, and browser-chrome colors.

findings.summary: The stylesheet does not adapt to contrast or forced-colors preferences.
findings.evidence: The CSS probe found no prefers-contrast or forced-colors rules; the emulated high-contrast capture remained unchanged.
findings.suggestedFix: Add forced-colors and prefers-contrast adaptations for borders, focus indicators, controls, and scroll affordances.

findings.summary: Navigation uses abrupt cross-document swaps rather than progressive View Transitions.
findings.evidence: CSS inspection across the loaded page found no view-transition declarations; representative routes are conventional MPA navigations.
findings.suggestedFix: Add @view-transition { navigation: auto } and stable view-transition-name values, with reduced-motion handling.

findings.summary: The persistent mobile chrome does not communicate scroll state.
findings.evidence: Mobile captures and CSS inspection show a fixed header but no scroll-state container query or progress indicator.
findings.suggestedFix: Use scroll-state queries or a lightweight progress affordance so persistent chrome responds to position.

findings.summary: A large service-closure notice blocks the marketplace on every homepage load.
findings.evidence: Desktop and mobile initial-load screenshots show a modal covering the primary content before any user action. The message is important, but the interruption occupies most of the viewport.
findings.suggestedFix: Move the persistent closure notice into prominent in-flow content, or remember dismissal and reserve a modal for the first high-risk action.

findings.summary: The blocking notice is an ad-hoc div modal without dialog semantics.
findings.evidence: The live DOM probe found visible .c-modal-* divs with no role=dialog, aria-modal, or native dialog element.
findings.suggestedFix: Implement the blocking notice with <dialog>, an accessible name, focus containment/restoration, Escape handling, and declarative close actions.

findings.summary: Responsive behavior is viewport-centric rather than component-aware.
findings.evidence: The loaded stylesheet probe found no @container rules even though cards and navigation components recur in narrow and wide contexts.
findings.suggestedFix: Introduce container queries for reusable card grids and navigation groups where their allocated width, not the viewport, determines layout.

findings.summary: Several interactive targets are too small for reliable touch use.
findings.evidence: The interaction probe found 12 visible controls below 24 CSS px in one dimension, including a 16x16 modal close button and 16-18px-high links.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide at least 24x24 CSS px targets, preferably 44x44 for primary touch controls, while retaining visible :focus-visible styles.

findings.summary: Mobile load performance is poor.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured performance 40, FCP 4.5s, LCP 8.0s, Speed Index 7.3s, and TTI 10.8s. A less-throttled trace measured LCP 2.28s, confirming network/CPU sensitivity.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the LCP element, reduce initial script and third-party work, and defer non-critical recommendations and analytics.

findings.summary: Late content causes severe layout movement.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported CLS 0.403 with three shifts; the mobile layout primitive independently observed CLS 0.317 from shifts at about 3.26s and 4.89s. The image audit found 95/100 images without explicit dimensions.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve dimensions/aspect-ratio for images, banners, recommendations, and the closure notice before asynchronous content arrives.

findings.summary: Render-blocking and poorly cached resources delay the initial page.
findings.evidence: The HAR identified parser-inserted styles and multiple classic scripts; the DOM confirmed the first-party scripts have neither async nor defer. Lighthouse estimated 2.13s render-blocking savings and 581KiB cache-lifetime savings.
findings.suggestedFix: Inline only critical CSS, defer non-critical classic scripts, break dependency chains, compress JSON responses, and apply long immutable caching to versioned assets.

findings.summary: The page ships substantial unused and duplicated script work.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 278KiB unused JavaScript and 34KiB unused CSS. Four Google tag loader requests alone transferred about 578KiB.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove duplicate tag containers, code-split page-specific features, and load recommendation/history code only when its surface is approached.

findings.summary: Many links and images lack accessible names.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed link-name; the DOM probe listed at least 20 visible unnamed interactive elements, and the image audit found 21 images without alt text.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every linked card one discernible name, use meaningful alt text or alt="" for decorative images, and remove redundant unnamed nested links.

findings.summary: Some text and UI colors fail WCAG contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse accessibility failed the color-contrast audit on the homepage.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust muted gray and red-on-light token pairs to meet 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text and essential UI.

findings.summary: Heading structure and modal focus semantics are inconsistent.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed heading-order; the DOM has an empty H1 followed by H3 navigation headings. The modal is not exposed as a dialog, although the sampled keyboard focus outline was visible.
findings.suggestedFix: Use one descriptive H1, sequential section headings and landmarks, and move/restore focus when the dialog opens/closes.

findings.summary: Asset markup does not consistently reserve image geometry and uses a deprecated API.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported unsized images and one deprecated API warning; the image primitive found 95 of 100 images without width and height.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit intrinsic width/height or aspect-ratio for every image and replace the deprecated API identified in the Lighthouse details.

findings.summary: The page has avoidable browser-platform hygiene failures.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported a BFCache blocker and missing source maps for large first-party JavaScript in addition to the deprecation warning.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the BFCache blocking behavior, publish production source maps to authorized tooling, and migrate deprecated code.

findings.summary: Many prominent card links have no descriptive link text.
findings.evidence: The DOM probe found at least 20 visible unnamed links and Lighthouse failed link-name. URLs are real hrefs and a viewport meta exists, but link purpose is not exposed reliably.
findings.suggestedFix: Give card anchors descriptive accessible text and avoid empty image-only link wrappers.

findings.summary: The site does not expose a sitemap at the conventional location.
findings.evidence: robots.txt returned 200 and allows primary content, while /sitemap.xml returned HTTP 404. Canonical URLs are present.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish and reference an XML sitemap covering canonical public listing, shop, article, and notice URLs.

findings.summary: Share metadata exists, but rich entity metadata is absent.
findings.evidence: The homepage has Open Graph tags but the DOM probe found no JSON-LD for the Organization/WebSite or marketplace entities.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate JSON-LD for Organization and WebSite, then Product/Offer or ItemList on matching detail/listing pages.

findings.summary: Core browser security headers are missing and analytics cookies are not Secure.
findings.evidence: HTTPS is used, but the headers primitive found no CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy. All eight observed cookies were flagged, including three Google Analytics cookies without Secure and with SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy HSTS, a nonce/hash-based CSP, nosniff, strict referrer and permissions policies; mark HTTPS cookies Secure and narrow SameSite/domain/lifetime.

findings.summary: Tracking and third-party delivery dominate the page load.
findings.evidence: The HAR recorded 71/79 requests and 1.318MB/1.435MB as cross-origin by host classification; tracker evidence found two known tracker origins. Four tag-manager/gtag files transferred about 578KiB before user interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Consolidate analytics, gate non-essential tracking on consent, batch events, and self-host or eliminate dependencies that do not provide direct user value.

findings.summary: The observed sign-in entry does not advertise phishing-resistant authentication.
findings.evidence: No permission prompt was triggered on load, but the d Account redirect presented ID-first sign-in and the rendered/auth source probe found no WebAuthn or PublicKeyCredential signal.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer passkey/WebAuthn authentication and conditional mediation alongside recovery-compatible fallbacks, clearly surfaced in the d Account flow.

findings.summary: Image delivery leaves meaningful byte and stability savings.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 316KiB image-delivery savings; the image probe found missing intrinsic dimensions on 95 images and no responsive source on the raster image it flagged.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve correctly sized AVIF/WebP variants with srcset/sizes and explicit dimensions, and prioritize only the LCP image.

Fix LCP, render-blocking delivery, duplicate analytics, and unused code
Reserve image and async-content geometry to eliminate CLS
Add accessible names, heading structure, contrast, modal focus, and adequate target sizes
Deploy missing security headers and tighten cookie policy
Add system preference themes and contrast adaptations
Publish sitemap and structured entity metadata
Modernize responsive and navigation transitions progressively
Offer passkey authentication in the d Account journey
Resolve BFCache, deprecation, and source-map hygiene issues
